- THE WALL: FireSegment clones every SPACING 6 studs along the line (X of CFrame.lookAt(line, line + dir)), each stretched every frame: Base (the flame bed, up to 4 high), Low / Mid / High (three Neon sheets, 30 / 35 / 35% of the height, less opaque toward the top), Flames (an invisible part the size of the wall whose emitters Fire / Smoke / Embers have Shape Box + ShapeStyle Volume, so they fill the wall whatever its height; their Rate is scaled with the height), Light (one in three segments keeps its PointLight). Held = it sinks to EMBER_HEIGHT 2.5 (fast: rate 5), let go = it roars back up (rate 9) with FireRoar and a small shake.
- THE BURN (server, every frame, only while nobody holds the lever and it is past EMERGE and before the fade): anyone within WALL_THICK 3 of the line, under its height + 3 = K.Strike for WALL_DAMAGE 28 x strength (strength = WEAKEST 0.4 + 0.6 x height / 140) and a shove back the way it came from (SHOVE 18 x strength back, HOP 20 up; it was 34 back + 26 up and threw people off their plates), HIT_COOLDOWN 2. Nobody on the lever the whole event: 74-88 damage per player in the bench.
- THE LEVER: on a random plate, K.TopCentre(plate) - dir x HOLDER_BACK / 2, facing the door (-Z of the model toward the fire). Prompt "Grab the lever" (GRAB_HOLD 0.4, REACH 9) at its top, on from 2 s. Grab = ONE holder: put at leverFrame * (0, root height, HOLDER_BACK 3.25) facing the lever (character:PivotTo), WalkSpeed and Jump x0 (Stats modifiers SwitchHoldWalk / SwitchHoldJump), the prompt off. Let go (release(why): soon / late / missed / letgo / knocked (KNOCKED_OFF 4 studs from the spot) / dead; "end" when the fire dies = no jam) = the modifiers off, JAM_TIME 5 s with the prompt off, Signal "Slip". The visual: the Arm group turns on a spring (UP -30 degrees, DOWN 62 degrees, sub-stepped), it shakes while held, rattles + Heat glows + Smoke while jammed, Sparks on letting go; a chain (one code part) from ChainRing over the plate's edge toward the door.
- THE STRUGGLE (server-judged, the fiddle's pattern): Signal "Cue"(userId, index, at) = a ring that reaches the circle at `at` (server clock); FIRST_RING 0.6 after grabbing, CUE_LEAD 1.1 to close in, RING_GAP_MIN 0.4 / MAX 1.1 between a good press and the next ring. The holder's client sends self:Send("Pull", index, FX.Now()); the server clamps the claimed time to [now - 1, now + 0.1] and judges: no ring on screen yet = ignored; earlier than at - EARLY 0.32 = "soon"; up to at + LATE 0.28 = good (Signal "Good", next ring); later = "late"; nothing by at + LATE + GRACE 0.35 = "missed". self:Send("LetGo") = "letgo".
- THE PANEL (LeverGui, cloned with FX.Gui onto the HOLDER's screen only, Call "Held"(userId, jammedUntil)): Panel > Scale, Plate > Title, Target (the circle: a button) > Zone (its rim, gold while a press would count), Ring (sized 1.9 -> 1 by the code), Key ("SPACE", "TAP" on a touch screen); Status; LetGo. Keys: SPACE, E, gamepad A / R2, a click / tap on Target (not using `processed`, chat typing skipped). Feedback right away on the client ("GOOD!" + SwitchGood + a tiny shake / "TOO SOON!" / "TOO LATE!"), the server decides. A phone (screen under PHONE_BELOW 500 px high): Scale max(0.62, h / 560), at the bottom 14 px up.
- THE ANIMATION: SwitchStruggle, 1.6 s loop, whole body, priority Action, played by the holder's OWN client on their character (so everybody sees it; FX.Animations: the KeyframeSequence in Studio, the uploaded id in ANIMATIONS (KEEP Animations) in the game). Solved in animgen/switch_anims.py: both fists (FIST = arm-local (0, -0.8, 0)) on the T-grip at +-0.58 of the lever held DOWN (axle PIVOT_Y 2.4, GRIP 3.2 up the arm, DOWN 62 degrees), the root HOLDER_BACK 3.25 behind the lever's foot; the torso leans back 9-23 degrees with a heave every loop, legs braced, and since R6 arms are rigid (a fist is always 1.39 studs from its shoulder) the hips slide 0.1-0.46 studs to keep the grip in reach (worst error 0.07 studs). LOOKED at: animgen/switch_sheet.py (contact sheet with the lever drawn).
- TOASTS: one at the start ("The door to hell is open! Grab the lever and hold the fire down."), one for whoever gets the item. Everything else is on the panel.
- SOUNDS (KEEP SOUNDS of deadswitch): LeverClank, FireRoar, ChainRattle (as before), NEW HellDoorGrind, HellDoorOpen, SwitchGood, SwitchSlip (Roblox stand-ins).
- MY CALLS, told in INSTALL.md: back-and-forth sweeps (CROSSING), the burn and the shove weaker as it dies down (WEAKEST), the smaller shove, one holder at a time, every letting go jams it, the holder put behind the lever (for the animation), LET GO, the start toast.

### 46.5 Rules learned
- RULE ONE AND THE FRAMEWORK: a server Call to a method named Done, Init or Step never reaches the client module (FX.Module keeps those three for itself: Done runs when the visual is DESTROYED). Name the server's "it's over" call something else (Over).
- A MOVE OF A WHOLE MODEL every frame for something that only moves at the start and the end (the door): only place it while it moves.
- A STRUGGLE / QTE HE CALLS EASY = one button (SPACE, E, a click, a tap), a big window (about 0.6 s), a ring you can read, the server judging the time the client claims (clamped), early presses while the ring is on screen count as mistakes (so mashing fails), presses before any ring shows are ignored.
- AN ANIMATION THAT HOLDS SOMETHING IN THE WORLD: the server puts the player exactly where the animation was solved for (PivotTo), and the animation tool solves the arms onto the grip frame by frame (R6 arms are rigid: let the hips slide).

### 47.5 Rules learned
- HIS STANDING ORDER (47.0 point 2): EVERY HUMANOID = AN R6 CHARACTER, animated with R6 KeyframeSequences he uploads. Build the rig from animgen (r6anim's JOINTS = the C0 / C1 the animations are solved with), weld the looks on, play with FX.Actor (an NPC) or the player's own Animator (a player).
- "SAME FUNCTION, NEW VISUALS" = his server script is not touched at all (it rides along in the package to carry the new models; the installer reports it unchanged); in his client keep the hit check exactly, run it first, and put everything that only draws inside a pcall after it.
- A MODEL FOR HIS OLD-STYLE VISUAL takes the name his server shows (Pulse), so the framework clones it as the visual: no server change needed. Say so in the model's header.
- A GHOST THAT STARES AT YOU: client-side visuals may differ per client: let each one face its own player.
- AN ANIMATION TIMED TO A SERVER MOMENT: start it its own lead time early (SCREAM_LEAD = the snap's time inside the animation), so the peak lands on the moment.

And `without its models`: Door / Ghost / Treat taken out of EventAssets: the porch is built in code on the plate and on the screen, no errors.
- THE BENCH DRAWS A VIEWPORTFRAME NOW: E.viewShot(name, player, viewportRec[, screen]) (tests/lib.luau) writes view_<name>.json (Scene.dumpView: the ViewportFrame's CurrentCamera, its light and ImageTransparency, every part in it), world_<name>.json (the world through the player's own camera) and gui_<name>.json; tools/render_view.py draws what a Camera sees (exact CFrame and FieldOfView, the ViewportFrame's Ambient / LightColor / LightDirection, see-through background; normals turned outwards); tools/compose_view.py puts the three together = that player's whole screen. THE BENCH'S CAMERA DOES NOT FOLLOW THE CHARACTER (48.4): the test puts each knocker's camera behind them, on their door.

### 49.5 Rules learned
- "REMOVE THE GUI THAT POPS UP, MAKE THE VIEWPORTFRAME WORK" = the window around a ViewportFrame goes, the ViewportFrame stays ON ITS OWN (see-through, no box, no text) and is built so it cannot stay empty: a Camera INSIDE it as its CurrentCamera (set again once on screen, checked every frame), the parts in a WorldModel, nothing inside it that a ViewportFrame cannot draw (lights, emitters, sounds; a BillboardGui inside one floats in the real world). His "toast" is K.Tell: a "GUI that pops up" is not a toast.
- A SEE-THROUGH ViewportFrame MUST NEVER LET A PART REACH ITS EDGE (it would be cut off by an invisible line): the bench projects every visible part through its camera, all through the animation.
- A 3D THING ON THE SCREEN DOES NOT SIT ON TOP OF THE REAL THING IT SHOWS: the knocker's real door is in the middle of his screen (the toast under it), so the screen's door is on the right. LOOK at the WHOLE screen (tools/compose_view.py) before deciding where a GUI goes.
- ONE MODEL FOR THE WORLD AND THE SCREEN: what stands on the plate is the same model that is cloned into the ViewportFrame; a group that turns (a door) has its own Root = the pivot, read by the code, so he can move it in Studio.

- Client (Client.client.lua): on Activated, only if Charges > 0, its own 1.5 s cooldown passed, Humanoid.FloorMaterial == Air and the humanoid's OWN jump is > 0.5 (UseJumpPower ? JumpPower : sqrt(2 g JumpHeight): a "no jumping" Stats modifier stops it): root vertical velocity = that jump, ChangeState(Jumping), FireServer("Puff"). The jump is on the client (the character's network owner): instant, and the server only counts.

### 51.4 Bench and tools
- tests/t_batchE.luau `bottle` (12 checks): in ServerStorage > Items; all parts welded, none anchored; held with 3 charges; nothing on the ground; in the air: a charge used, the jump higher (one jump 6.8 studs; popped 0.3 s into a jump: 12.6), a CloudPuff in the workspace, gone a moment later; two clicks in one jump = one charge; Stats Jump x0 then 14 studs up in the air: nothing; the last charge destroys the tool; no script errors.

- The other numbers: 51.1.

### 51.5 Rules learned
- AN ITEM IS A TOOL IN ServerStorage > Items, made his way: a Server script (getOwner / getAlive / its own RemoteEvent ItemRemote) + a LocalScript Client for anything the player's own character must do at once (a jump, a dash: the client owns the character), state on the tool as attributes. Its looks are real parts WELDED to the Handle (unanchored, massless, no collisions), effects it leaves in the world are templates welded and invisible inside it.
- A MOVEMENT ITEM USES THE PLAYER'S OWN STAT (the Humanoid's jump as it is right now), so his Stats modifiers (a "no jumping" trick) still win.

### 54.5 Rules learned
- "DO N EVENTS IN ONE GO" = one update holding N backlog pieces, all tested together; deliver it whole.
- "NOT GENTLE RAIN! DONT DO IT TO GENTLE RAIN!": a change he asks for across "the events that ..." never touches Gentle Rain; when his words name a group, list which events I put in it, in one line, BEFORE changing them.
- A STAT BUFF FROM AN EVENT = his StatShift (StatShift.Give: Stats modifier, whole match, no duplicates, opposites cancel) through K.Boon; a new boon's Id / Name must not contain a word of StatShift's DEFAULT_OPPOSES (heart, feather, maat, hermes, tartarus, veil, nighthunt) or styx, or it cancels a real stat shift.
- "PROTECTED" / "CAN'T BE DESTROYED" = inside PlateSpawner.DestroyPlate (every plate-breaking event goes through it), never in the one event.
- A server-side thing on a plate (a prompt, a tray) = K.Pin to it; a client visual on a plate = FX.OnPlate (it rides the plate's TOP).

### 99.1 StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/EventClients/EventVisualsClient
<<<SOURCE StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/EventClients/EventVisualsClient | LocalScript | 225 lines | HIS STUDIO COPY, pasted by him on Oct 7 2026. Not changed in that session. Do not write another one; build on it.
````lua
-- LocalScript: StarterPlayer > StarterPlayerScripts > EventClients > EventVisualsClient
-- Client side of event visuals. The server says what to show; this builds it locally
-- (from ReplicatedStorage > EventAssets > <EventId>) and animates it, so it's smooth
-- and costs the server nothing.
--
-- Optional per-event behaviour lives in ReplicatedStorage > EventClients > <EventId>
-- (a ModuleScript). Any of these functions are used if present:
--   Build(assetName, props) -> Instance   placeholder to use when the asset doesn't exist
--   Spawned(instance, state, props)      right after it's built
--   Render(instance, state, base, dt)    every frame; if present, it's in charge of positioning
--   <AnyMethod>(instance, state, ...)    when the server calls Visuals.Call(id, "AnyMethod", ...)
--   Destroyed(instance, state)
-- `state` is a table you can keep anything in for that visual.

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local remote = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Remotes"):WaitForChild("EventVisuals") :: RemoteEvent
local assets = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("EventAssets")

local folder = workspace:FindFirstChild("ClientEventVisuals")
if not folder then
	folder = Instance.new("Folder")
	folder.Name = "ClientEventVisuals"
	folder.Parent = workspace
end

type Visual = {
	Instance: PVInstance,
	Module: any,
	State: { [string]: any },
	Base: CFrame,
	Dirty: boolean,
	Tween: { From: CFrame, To: CFrame, Start: number, Time: number, Style: Enum.EasingStyle, Direction: Enum.EasingDirection }?,
}
local visuals: { [number]: Visual } = {}
local modules: { [string]: any } = {}

local function getModule(eventId: string): any
	if modules[eventId] ~= nil then
		return modules[eventId] or nil
	end
	local container = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("EventClients")
	local moduleScript = container and container:FindFirstChild(eventId)
	if moduleScript and moduleScript:IsA("ModuleScript") then
		local ok, result = pcall(require, moduleScript)
		if ok then
			modules[eventId] = result
			return result
		end
		warn("[EventVisualsClient] " .. eventId .. " module failed: " .. tostring(result))
	end
	if not moduleScript then
		warn(("[EventVisualsClient] No client module for '%s'. Add a ModuleScript named '%s' in ReplicatedStorage > EventClients"):format(eventId, eventId))
	end
	modules[eventId] = false
	return nil
end

local function call(visual: Visual, method: string, ...)
	local fn = visual.Module and visual.Module[method]
	if fn then
		local ok, err = pcall(fn, visual.Instance, visual.State, ...)
		if not ok then
			warn(("[EventVisualsClient] %s failed: %s"):format(method, tostring(err)))
		end
	end
end

local function prepare(instance: Instance)
	local parts = if instance:IsA("BasePart") then { instance } else {}
	for _, descendant in instance:GetDescendants() do
		if descendant:IsA("BasePart") then
			table.insert(parts, descendant)
		end
	end
	for _, part in parts do
		part.Anchored = true
		part.CanCollide = false
		part.CanQuery = false
		part.CanTouch = false
	end
end

local function build(eventId: string, asset: string, props, module): PVInstance?
	if asset == "@Circle" then
		local radius = props.Radius or 4
		local circle = Instance.new("Part")
		circle.Name = "WarningCircle"
		circle.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
		circle.Size = Vector3.new(0.2, radius * 2, radius * 2)
		circle.Color = props.Color or Color3.fromRGB(200, 30, 40)
		circle.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
		circle.Transparency = props.Transparency or 0.55
		return circle
	end

	local eventFolder = assets:FindFirstChild(eventId)
	local source = eventFolder and eventFolder:FindFirstChild(asset)
	if not source or not source:IsA("PVInstance") then
		-- No model yet: let the event's client module build a placeholder
		if module and module.Build then
			local ok, placeholder = pcall(module.Build, asset, props)
			if ok and placeholder then
				return placeholder
			end
		end
		warn(("[EventVisualsClient] Missing asset %s/%s"):format(eventId, asset))
		return nil
	end
	local instance = source:Clone()
	for attribute in instance:GetAttributes() do
		instance:SetAttribute(attribute, nil)
	end
	return instance
end

-- Circles lie flat: the cylinder's length runs along X, so tip it up
local function placementFor(asset: string, cframe: CFrame): CFrame
	if asset == "@Circle" then
		return cframe * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90))
	end
	return cframe
end

local handlers = {}

function handlers.Spawn(id: number, eventId: string, asset: string, cframe: CFrame, props)
	if visuals[id] then
		return
	end
	local module = if asset:sub(1, 1) == "@" then nil else getModule(eventId)
	local instance = build(eventId, asset, props or {}, module)
	if not instance then
		return
	end
	prepare(instance)
	local base = placementFor(asset, cframe)
	instance:PivotTo(base)
	instance.Parent = folder

	local visual: Visual = {
		Instance = instance,
		Module = module,
		State = { Asset = asset },
		Base = base,
		Dirty = false,
		Tween = nil,
	}
	visuals[id] = visual
	call(visual, "Spawned", props or {})
end

function handlers.Move(id: number, cframe: CFrame)
	local visual = visuals[id]
	if visual then
		visual.Tween = nil
		visual.Base = placementFor(visual.State.Asset, cframe)
		visual.Dirty = true
	end
end

function handlers.Tween(id: number, cframe: CFrame, duration: number, style: string, direction: string)
	local visual = visuals[id]
	if visual then
		visual.Tween = {
			From = visual.Base,
			To = placementFor(visual.State.Asset, cframe),
			Start = os.clock(),
			Time = math.max(duration, 0.001),
			Style = (Enum.EasingStyle :: any)[style] or Enum.EasingStyle.Quad,
			Direction = (Enum.EasingDirection :: any)[direction] or Enum.EasingDirection.Out,
		}
	end
end

function handlers.Call(id: number, method: string, ...)
	local visual = visuals[id]
	if visual then
		call(visual, method, ...)
	end
end

function handlers.Destroy(id: number)
	local visual = visuals[id]
	if visual then
		visuals[id] = nil
		call(visual, "Destroyed")
		visual.Instance:Destroy()
	end
end

remote.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(kind: string, ...)
	local handler = handlers[kind]
	if handler then
		handler(...)
	end
end)

RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function(dt)
	for _, visual in visuals do
		local tween = visual.Tween
		if tween then
			local alpha = math.clamp((os.clock() - tween.Start) / tween.Time, 0, 1)
			visual.Base = tween.From:Lerp(tween.To, TweenService:GetValue(alpha, tween.Style, tween.Direction))
			visual.Dirty = true
			if alpha >= 1 then
				visual.Tween = nil
			end
		end

		local render = visual.Module and visual.Module.Render
		if render then
			local ok, err = pcall(render, visual.Instance, visual.State, visual.Base, dt)
			if not ok then
				warn("[EventVisualsClient] Render failed: " .. tostring(err))
				visual.Module = nil
			end
		elseif visual.Dirty then
			visual.Instance:PivotTo(visual.Base)
			visual.Dirty = false
		end
	end
end)
````
<<<END SOURCE StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/EventClients/EventVisualsClient

### 99.2 ServerScriptService/Systems/EventUtil
<<<SOURCE ServerScriptService/Systems/EventUtil | ModuleScript | 1985 lines | [v41] AS DELIVERED IN OCT 12 UPDATE 27 (his Oct 8 export copy + at the bottom: BaseTop, Border, RingSpot, Chest (38.4), Box, Beside, RingAlong, WaterY (39.4); K.Dot marks the status; Show sends EventName, Listen (43.4)).
